name: Pituitary Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for Pituitary Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of pituitary mass on MRI or CT imaging
Biochemical evidence of pituitary hormone hypersecretion or hyposecretion
Symptoms attributable to mass effect or hormonal imbalance such as visual field defects or amenorrhea

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological identification of pituitary mass plus biochemical evidence of hormonal dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other sellar masses and correlation with clinical presentation.

searchTerms: enlarged facial features from growth hormone excess
coarse facial appearance
prominent jaw and brow due to acromegaly

frontal or eye socket headaches

menstrual cycle irregularities

blurred or decreased eyesight
difficulty seeing clearly

increased body weight due to hypothyroidism
slow metabolism causing weight increase

hypogonadism with decreased libido
reduced sexual desire due to hormone deficiency
high blood pressure from cortisol excess
hypertension due to steroid hormone
blood pressure raised by cortisol

occasional.notes: Rare in pituitary adenomas but possible in invasive tumors

laboratory: Increased IGF-1 in growth hormone-secreting tumors
Elevated cortisol or ACTH in corticotroph adenomas
Low levels of pituitary hormones in hypopituitarism
imaging: MRI showing sellar mass with or without suprasellar extension
CT scan may show sellar enlargement or calcifications
genetic: Mutations in AIP gene in familial isolated pituitary adenomas
MEN1 gene mutations in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1
other: Visual field testing demonstrating bitemporal hemianopsia

distinguishingFeatures: More common in children and adolescents
Non-enhancing cystic lesion in sellar region

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with visual loss (pituitary apoplexy)
